summary: Kaigen Noritake works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo and held an assistant professorship at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. He taught at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho universities, and led Shiba Junior and Senior High School.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at Komazawa, Keio, and First Higher School, he lectured at Harvard (~1912–1913) and served as Komazawa University's head teacher (1919) and first president (1921; 1925–1934).
Kaiun Shiradate specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University, serving as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and later as a professor (attested 1999–2002).
Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Sogen Omori, and later held a post at Sophia University.

Kakushō Ujiie (d. 1985) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He conducted research studies at Tribhuvan University (attested 1970) and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1970 and 1984–1985).

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Scottish Church College (~1908–1912) and the University of Calcutta (~1912–1914), later holding posts at Scottish Church College (~1915–1919) and Calcutta (~1923–1955).

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and master. He studied at Palpung Monastery under teachers including Lama Norbu Tondrup. He served as Vajra Master at Palpung (~1942–1955) and abbot of Changchub Choeling Monastery (1957).
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar works in Indology and Sinology. He studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and became professor emeritus at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).

Kamala Tiyavanich works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there in 1993–1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. During his academic career, he held posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Charles University (1946–1952) and held positions at the Czech Oriental Institute (1952–1970), Charles University (~1960–1968), and Utrecht University (~1976–1992).

Kamla Chowdhry (1920–2006) studied at Santiniketan, the University of the Punjab, the University of Calcutta (~1943–1945), and Michigan State University (~1947–1949). She held posts at Harvard University and the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi (1935–2021) was an Indologist who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidasa Akademi, and Advisor to the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Holyoke College and completed her PhD at the University of Virginia (~2002–2009) under David Germano and Paul Groner. She held a post at Muhlenberg College (2011).
Kan Hang (b. 1965) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Su Bai and served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed a PhD at the University of Peradeniya under Sirima Kiribamune (~1964–1968), later lecturing in Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982).
Kanchu Onoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He taught as an instructor at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and later served as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974), completed his doctorate under Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976), and held a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

Kang-yuan Sung works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Calgary, where he earned an MA (attested 1999) under supervisor Anthony W. Barber and was taught by Leslie S. Kawamura.
